description.value: A prospective study examined clinical, demographic, and neuroimaging predictors distinguishing primary psychiatric disorders from probable/definite behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia after 2 years of follow-up.

spans.text: A major strength of this study is the inclusion of patients based on a symptom profile with late-onset behavioral change

description.value: Multicenter prospective study with baseline assessment and 2-year follow-up.

spans.text: The LOF study is a multicenter prospective study conducted between April 2011 and June 2015.
Patients were recruited from the Amsterdam Dementia Cohort16 and the GGZInGeest Department of Old Age Psychiatry, Amsterdam, The Netherlands.

spans.text: For the current study, we selected patients with a 2-year follow-up multidisciplinary diagnosis of a primary psychiatric disorder (n = 46) or probable/definite bvFTD (n = 27)

value: Late-onset behavioral symptoms dominating the clinical presentation; age 45–75 years; Frontal Behavioral Inventory score ≥11 or Stereotypy Rating Inventory score ≥10; 2-year follow-up multidisciplinary diagnosis of a primary psychiatric disorder.

spans.text: Patients were eligible for inclusion when behavioral symptoms dominated the clinical presentation, their score on the Frontal Behavioral Inventory (FBI)17 was ≥ 11 or the Stereotypy Rating Inventory (SRI)18 was ≥ 10, and they were aged between 45 and 75 years.

value: Possible bvFTD/phenocopy cases, death without postmortem verification or clear clinical diagnosis, and loss to follow-up were excluded from the final analysis.

spans.text: Three patients were diagnosed with a 2-year follow-up diagnosis of possible bvFTD, as no other explanation could be found for their symptoms, cases that may be considered as bvFTD phenocopies.

clinical_characteristics.value: Late-onset behavioral disturbances followed prospectively for 2 years; 4 of 27 bvFTD patients had definite bvFTD, including genetic or histopathologic confirmation.

spans.text: Of the 27 patients in the bvFTD group, 4 patients (5.5%) were diagnosed with definite bvFTD consisting of 2 with C9orf72 expansion hexanucleotide repeat, 1 with progranulin mutation, and 1 with histopathologically confirmed tauopathy (Table 1).
